claim: Section 10 likelihood-ratio ordering claim for the MGS(MGSD) distribution
quote: Prove that the MSG distribution complies with the ordering with the highest likelihood (the likelihood ratio ordering). Assume that X and Y are two independent Random variables with probability distribution function f_x(x; lambda, theta) and f_y(x; beta, alpha). If lambda < alpha and theta < beta, then Lambda = f_x(x;lambda,theta)/f_y(x;beta,alpha) = [theta^2 (beta+1) (lambda theta x^2/2 + (theta+x)/(theta^2+1))] / [alpha^2 (lambda+1) (beta alpha x^2/2 + (alpha+x)/(alpha^2+1))] e^{-(theta-alpha)x}. ... Hence, d log[Lambda]/dx < 0 if lambda < beta, theta < alpha.
model: other: two distributions of the same family
family: mixture of Gamma(3,theta) and Shanker(theta): f(x;lambda,theta) = theta^2/(lambda+1) * (lambda theta x^2/2 + (theta+x)/(theta^2+1)) e^{-theta x}
compared: X ~ MGS(lambda, theta) vs Y ~ MGS(beta, alpha) (parameter roles swapped in the paper's notation)

hypotheses.text: If lambda < alpha and theta < beta (statement); conclusion requires lambda < beta, theta < alpha (as printed)
hypotheses.formal: inconsistent parameter inequalities between hypothesis and conclusion

conclusion.direction: X <=_LR Y (likelihood-ratio ordering, density ratio decreasing)

ambiguity: Heavily garbled/inconsistent: hypothesis says lambda < alpha, theta < beta while the conclusion condition reads lambda < beta, theta < alpha; only the lr order is claimed (not hr/mrl/st). Parameter symbols switch roles between the two distributions (theta vs alpha as rate, lambda vs beta as mixing weight). No proof rigor; differentiation shown without justification of sign.
